questions.question: What is the safest general approach to an acute hot, swollen, painful joint?
choices: Assume recurrent gout if the patient has a prior history
Treat septic arthritis as a critical alternative until appropriately excluded
Start an outpatient steroid course before assessing infection risk
Wait for fever to occur before evaluating
questions.explanation: Septic arthritis can threaten joint function and may present without fever, especially in high-risk patients. A hot swollen joint requires urgent assessment of infection alongside crystal and other causes.

questions.question: Which combination of symptoms with low-back pain is most concerning for cauda equina syndrome or severe neurologic compromise?
choices: Pain that improves with rest
New urinary retention, saddle sensory loss, and progressive bilateral leg weakness
Mild stiffness after exercise
Pain limited to one paraspinal muscle
questions.explanation: New urinary retention or overflow incontinence, saddle anesthesia, bowel dysfunction, and progressive/global lower-extremity weakness require emergency evaluation.

questions.question: What is the appropriate sequence for a focused extremity examination?
choices: Look, feel, move, and assess function while comparing sides
Order imaging before examining the patient
Test only the painful side
Begin with a forced passive range-of-motion maneuver
questions.explanation: Inspect, palpate, assess safe range of motion, and evaluate function while comparing both sides. Include distal neurovascular status when relevant.

questions.question: Why should an FNP not automatically reassure an older patient who cannot bear weight after a fall when initial radiographs are negative?
choices: Radiographs are never useful
Occult fracture or other clinically important injury can remain possible when history and function are concerning
All pain after a fall is due to arthritis
Advanced imaging is prohibited after negative films
questions.explanation: A negative initial radiograph does not always exclude occult fracture. Persistent inability to bear weight and risk context require safe disposition and pathway-based reassessment.

questions.question: Which finding after extremity trauma requires immediate emergency evaluation for possible limb-threatening compromise?
choices: Stable mild soreness only with movement
Progressively escalating pain with tense swelling, sensory change, and pain on passive stretch
A superficial bruise that is not enlarging
Pain that improves with rest and normal function
questions.explanation: Escalating disproportionate pain, tense swelling, pain with passive stretch, paresthesia, pallor, paralysis, or pulselessness can indicate compartment or neurovascular compromise.

questions.question: Which statement about laboratory tests in acute monoarthritis is most accurate?
choices: A normal serum uric acid level rules out gout and infection
Serum uric acid alone identifies the cause of any hot joint
Laboratory tests provide context but cannot alone exclude septic arthritis; synovial-fluid analysis may be needed
No testing is useful in a painful swollen joint
questions.explanation: Serum studies cannot independently exclude septic arthritis or establish the cause of an acutely inflamed joint. Aspiration may be required when infection or crystal disease is a key question.

questions.question: Which history feature is a red flag for potentially complicated low-back pain?
choices: Brief pain after an unusual workout that is steadily improving
Fever, immune compromise, or history of cancer with persistent back pain
A prior self-limited muscle strain
Pain relieved by a comfortable position without other symptoms
questions.explanation: Fever, immune compromise, cancer history, trauma/osteoporosis risk, progressive neurologic deficit, and bowel/bladder or saddle symptoms warrant evaluation for serious causes.

questions.question: Why is medication reconciliation important in musculoskeletal assessment?
choices: Medications do not influence injury or joint presentations
Anticoagulants, corticosteroids, immunosuppressants, diuretics, and other drugs can change bleeding, infection, fracture, crystal, fall, and treatment risk
Only over-the-counter medications matter
It replaces the physical examination
questions.explanation: Medication exposure changes both diagnostic risk and treatment safety. Confirm all prescribed, OTC, supplement, and substance exposures.

questions.question: What is the best role of imaging in a musculoskeletal evaluation?
choices: Replace emergency transfer when a limb is threatened
Answer a specific structural question, selected by mechanism, examination, urgency, and local pathway
Obtain MRI for every uncomplicated back-pain complaint
Use one normal image to overrule concerning function and trajectory
questions.explanation: Imaging should answer a defined clinical question. It supports—rather than replaces—emergency disposition and serial clinical reasoning.

questions.question: What is essential in a safe outpatient musculoskeletal plan?
choices: A vague instruction to call if pain persists
Specific precautions for fever, worsening pain/swelling, neurologic or neurovascular change, inability to bear weight, bowel/bladder symptoms, and failure to improve
Avoiding follow-up to reduce testing
Assuming a familiar diagnosis cannot change
questions.explanation: Musculoskeletal presentations can evolve. Explicit precautions, safe mobility planning, test-result ownership, and reassessment protect against missed serious disease.
